info.name: 02 Resilient Delivery
info.description:
Workflow 2 test payloads.

Run order: 1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b.

Workflow must be PUBLISHED. Request 2 takes about 8 seconds because of the backoff, that is the point.

request.description:
Expect 200, status 'delivered', attempts 1.

The baseline. Everything after this is a failure mode.

The _demo_force_failure flag (gated behind demoMode, ignored in production) points the sender at an unreachable port so every attempt fails instantly.

Expect 502, status 'retries_exhausted', attempts 4 (1 initial + 3 retries).

WATCH IN N8N: the execution log shows Send Email running four times with Wait Before Retry between each, backing off 1s, 2s, 4s. Then a row appears in Dead_Letter, then the alert fires.

The response reports dead_letter_written and the alert outcome separately.

item.name: 3 - Validation failure -> dead letter, NO alert

request.description:
Missing contract_type and start_date, invalid email.

Expect 422 with all errors in one array, plus dead_letter_written: true.

The distinction that matters: this IS persisted, because nothing should be silently lost, but it does NOT page anyone. It is the caller's error to fix and cannot be replayed. Check the sheet: reason is validation_failed and alerted is not_required.

Expect n8n's OWN error: code 422, 'Failed to parse request body'.

This is correct and worth explaining on camera. n8n's HTTP layer parses the body before any node runs, so no node can catch this. Nothing crashes and nothing is half-processed.

Same broken body, but Content-Type is text/plain so n8n does not try to parse it.

Now it reaches the workflow. Expect 400, status 'invalid_json', with a correlation_id, produced by Validate and Normalise.

Run 4a and 4b back to back and say: I handle the case I can own, and I know where the boundary is.
